brief: Pots on my balcony for three hot chilli pepper seedlings.

requirements.requirement: Pots for three seedlings (three separate pots)
requirements.evidence: Three full-depth drained bins bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0, bin:0,1,0 (hex-bin-full-drain), one per cell, each soil-filled

requirements.requirement: Hot chilli pepper seedlings, three of them
requirements.evidence: Planted pepper-seedling prop:1, prop:2, prop:3 (seedling stage). No hot-chilli-specific prop exists in the catalogue (chilli search returned 0; only Sweet pepper) so the pepper species/variety and heat cannot be shown; the shape is a pepper seedling.

requirements.evidence: Open-top drained pots suit balcony growing and drainage, and caps/locked joints (capOpenFaces, lockJoints) finish the bases. The configurator cannot verify heat/UV/waterproofing or material suitability — parts are printed in a material the user chooses — so outdoor durability is not verified.

finish.summary: Built a compact cluster of three hex pots: three full bases each with a full-depth drained bin (hex-bin-full-drain), soil-filled and each planted with a pepper seedling (props 1-3), open faces capped and joints locked. Check is clear with no issues. Note: no hot-chilli-specific plant prop exists, so sweet-pepper seedlings stand in; and outdoor heat/UV resistance depends on the user's print material, which the configurator cannot verify.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Three chilli seedlings for the balcony — I'll build three soil-filled pots and plant them.
